svg.desc: A grid of deviation tier against coalition-only passage for 39 sampled laws where no challenge was found and 7 challenged Basic Laws coded under T1. Entrenches, coalition only: 1 with no challenge found, 0 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; None, coalition only: 1 with no challenge found, 0 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; Limited, coalition only: 3 with no challenge found, 2 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; Sharp, coalition only: 0 with no challenge found, 1 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; Entrenches, at least one opposition vote: 2 with no challenge found, 0 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; None, at least one opposition vote: 5 with no challenge found, 0 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; Limited, at least one opposition vote: 1 with no challenge found, 2 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; Entrenches, not known: 7 with no challenge found, 0 Adverse, 1 Not adverse; None, not known: 11 with no challenge found, 0 Adverse, 0 Not adverse; Limited, not known: 8 with no challenge found, 1 Adverse, 0 Not adverse.
svg.text: Where 46 coded Basic Laws sit on two axes of the sliding scale that Medina reads in the
Across: whether and how far the law contradicts the five democratic values, as the coders scored it. Down: whether any opposition
member voted for it. Each mark is one law.
Deviation tier, as coded: Entrenches and None contradict no value; Limited and Sharp contradict one (ordered steps, not distances)

svg.text: The scale: the sliding scale is Medina's reading of the Court's approach, which he presents as the article's main novelty (p. 681). In it, the
greater an amendment's departure from the unwritten constitution, the more stringent the procedural requirements, among them the majority needed
for enactment, the government's immediate interest and whether the amendment takes effect at once (pp. 702, 708). Neither axis here is a
distance. The tiers are ordered steps; positions inside a cell only keep the marks apart; and "at least one opposition vote" is not broad
support. Breadth needs the opposition's share of the vote, which is not yet recorded (issue 16).
Scope: Israel; laws titled Basic Law, 1958 to 2026. Laws: the 39 sampled laws where no challenge was found and the 7 challenged Basic Laws in the
codebook; the two 1969 statutes in the codebook are ordinary laws and are left out. Values coded from legislative records by coders who did not
open the judgments, though both reported seeing court outcomes in search snippets for four of the challenged laws (results.md); outcome-blindness
is not claimed for them. Coalition-only passage is not known where no record names the voters, mostly before October 2003.
